intro: Nottingham's oldest tree stands in Wollaton Park, the public park around the Elizabethan Wollaton Hall on the city's western edge. The Friends of Wollaton Park count more than five hundred oaks of at least ten species there, planted singly and in avenues, and single out one as ancient: the Arbour Oak on Arbour Hill, south-east of the Hall, pollarded in the seventeenth century and thought to date from the 1460s. A reader sent us its photograph, taken after snow.

location.address: Arbour Hill, Wollaton Park, Wollaton Road, Nottingham NG8 2AE

trees.story:
On Arbour Hill, south-east of Wollaton Hall, stands the oak the Friends of Wollaton Park think started life in the 1460s, more than a century before the Hall was built in 1588. Of the five hundred and more oaks in the park it is the one they single out as ancient.

It is a hybrid of the two native oaks, English and sessile, which the Friends name as Quercus x rosacea. In the seventeenth century it was pollarded: its branches were cut back again and again for wood, and the tree answered by throwing out the crowd of limbs it still carries.

A reader who sent us its photograph gives the girth as nearly 7 metres and the spread of the crown as about 40 metres. Their picture was taken after snow. A short, swollen trunk splits a little above head height into a dozen heavy limbs that twist outwards and upwards, every one of them lined with snow, the low winter sun catching the bark at the top. A wooden fence and a stand of pines close in behind it.

Wollaton Park is the city's public park around the Hall, and the oak stands in it. If you have measured it yourself, tell us here.

trees.verify_notes: 2026-11-16 session (Hidde asked for the open reader inbox): a reader's website tip (tip-839) with a photograph, no coordinate. The Friends of Wollaton Park oak leaflet (2025) names the Arbour Oak on Arbour Hill, Quercus x rosacea, thought to date from the 1460s, pollarded in the 17th century; their uMap tree survey (Colin Robbins, 2023, updated 2024 and 2025, from an NCC database) has 'Hybrid Oak (Arbour Oak)' at 52.943362, -1.203791 in the Oak layer, not in its Felled / Dead layer, which is the pin and the life check. Girth nearly 7 m and spread 40 m are the reader's. The reader's note reads like the Friends' own text, so it is used for facts, not quoted. Photograph viewed: the whole tree in snow, trunk and crown, daylight, colour; 480 px wide.
